title: Fpqc descent of properness for algebraic spaces over schemes
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism from an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering family of schemes [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Put $X_i=X\times_TT_i$ and let $f_i:X_i\to T_i$ be the projection [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $f$ is proper if and only if every $f_i$ is proper, with properness as in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]: separated, of finite type and universally closed. No finite-presentation, Noetherian, flatness, connectedness or nonemptiness assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0422, lemma-descending-property-proper, with Tag 03YH, definition-property-morphisms-local; restricted to a scheme target and scheme covering family.

proof.text: If $f$ is proper, apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] with $B=Y=T$, $Y'=T_i$ and $g=g_i$ for each $i$. The morphisms $T_i\to T$ need no extra hypotheses for this direction. Its conclusion is properness of every projection $f_i$ in the convention of that node. Separatedness (closed-immersion diagonal on every scheme test), local finite type on compatible etale scheme charts and universal closedness (closedness on point spaces after every algebraic-space base change) are stated identically there and in [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Quasi-compactness there means that every affine scheme base change $W$ admits a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme, while [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] asks that $|W|$ be compact; by [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] these agree: the final clause gives compactness of $|W|$ from such an atlas, and conversely, refining any atlas of $W$ by the affine opens of its source to a disjoint union of affine schemes, the first clause extracts a quasi-compact finite subatlas. Hence each $f_i$ is proper in the sense of the item, proving the forward implication.

source.place: Tag 0422, forward implication, using spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04WP (lemma-base-change-proper).

proof.text: Conversely assume every $f_i$ proper. By [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], each $f_i$ is separated and quasi-compact, is locally of finite type on compatible etale scheme charts, and is universally closed. We will descend these four properties separately; none asserts flatness of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0422, expand properness using spaces-morphisms.tex definition-proper (03ZM).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-qc-separated-descent] twice, once to quasi-compactness and once to separatedness, with the given scheme covering, taking the common base $S=T$. This gives both properties of $f$. The separatedness conventions in that statement and [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] are the identical closed-immersion diagonal test. For the quasi-compactness convention, [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas] gives the equivalence between compact point space and existence of a quasi-compact surjective etale scheme atlas: refine an atlas by its affine opens, extract its finite subatlas in the compact case; conversely the final clause of that node gives compactness from a quasi-compact atlas. Apply this on each affine scheme test to identify the two conventions.

source.place: Tags 041L (lemma-descending-property-quasi-compact) and 0421 (lemma-descending-property-separated); compatibility of the quasi-compactness conventions uses spaces-properties.tex lemma-quasi-compact-space.

proof.text: Use the fpqc-local-on-target clause of [lem-sfb-space-lft-smooth-fpqc-locality] for $f$ and the given covering. It gives local finite type of $f$. Its chartwise definition is exactly the local finite type clause of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. The scheme covering is also a covering in the scheme-pullback convention used by the locality node, since [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] says every scheme base change of it is fpqc. Combine local finite type with quasi-compactness from Step 3 to obtain finite type of $f$.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-fpqc-descend-universally-closed] to $f$ and this same scheme covering. All its hypotheses hold: each $f_i$ is universally closed by Step 2; there are no separation, flatness or finite-type hypotheses to supply. Thus $f$ is universally closed. Together with separatedness from Step 3 and finite type from Step 4 this is precisely properness by [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], proving the reverse implication.

source.place: Tag 0422, combining Tag 041O (lemma-descending-property-universally-closed) with separatedness and finite type.
